scope.lift: fixed Serre-Tate canonical lift with elliptic Teichmuller section in compatible coordinates

questions.formula: iota(a0,a1)=[a0]+p[a1]=u(a0)+p(C_p(a0)+a1) mod p^2; therefore d1(iota(a0,a1))=a1+C_p(a0) in F_p
questions.phase_relation: psi_{p^2}(iota(a0,a1))=psi_{p^2}(u(a0))*psi_p(d1); the primitive whole-Witt phase is not the ordinary-digit phase
questions.precision_one_control: the first coordinate is x, (x)_infinity=2[O], and x is not in K^p-K+F_p

questions.leading_coefficient: -2*A^(-1), with A the nonzero Hasse invariant in the source normalization
questions.representation_warning: Artin-Schreier equivalence in K is strictly finer than equality on affine F_p samples

questions.comparison: the source term exceeds the trivial cardinality bound for p>3, so the only effective normalized bound is 1
questions.primitive_W2_note: the distinct primitive phase attached to (x,x1) has the same numerical local coefficient 3p

questions.remainder: R_can is the unique degree-
questions.sample_relation: R_can(x(P))=F_can(x(P)) for every affine P in E(F_p)
questions.global_pole_result: the leading pole 3p-1 does not survive in R_can; its pole order is at most 2p-2
questions.AS_relation: F_can-R_can has reduced pole 3p-1 and is not in K^p-K, so F_can and R_can are not Artin-Schreier equivalent
questions.not_claimed: no minimum conductor over sample-equivalent representatives and no universal exact conductor for R_can

questions.pointwise_transfer: for n prime to p, finite etaleness gives a unique n-torsion lift on each fixed good-reduction model; on the canonical model the group-homomorphic tau(P) equals it
questions.universal_digit_identity: for any selected Witt x-coordinate (x,x1_s), d1=x1_s+C_p(x) pointwise
questions.open_boundary: prime-to-p torsion uniqueness does not identify global coordinates across different lift models; arbitrary good reduction supplies neither the canonical global section nor its degree/conductor
questions.source_converse: a global section regular away from O with deg x1<3p and deg y1<4p forces the lift and section to be canonical
